guarantees.claim: On async reset (rst_ni low), status_alert_fatal_fault is cleared to 0.
When alert_fatal is high and reset is inactive, status_alert_fatal_fault is set to 1.
When reset is inactive and alert_fatal is not high, status_alert_fatal_fault retains its previous value (sticky behavior).

assumptions.claim: alert_fatal must be a correctly synchronized, glitch-free signal representing a fatal fault condition.
assumptions.risk: A spurious or glitched alert_fatal will cause an irreversible sticky fault indication, potentially triggering inappropriate error handling or unnecessary reset.

assumptions.claim: The async reset rst_ni must be asserted and deasserted in compliance with timing requirements to avoid metastability in the status register.
assumptions.risk: Metastability could lead to functional corruption of the fault indicator.

uncertain_points.claim: status_alert_fatal_fault is sticky and only cleared by reset. If this signal is exposed as a CSR to software, there may be an expectation of software clearing (e.g., write-1-to-clear) that is not implemented here.
uncertain_points.risk: If clearing is expected but missing, the fault indication becomes permanent until system reset, potentially causing repeated error responses or blocking normal operation. If clearing is intentionally reset-only, the design intent needs confirmation.
